newsitem.title: GERMANY: Bonn urges Milosevic to recognise Zajedno wins.
newsitem.headline: Bonn urges Milosevic to recognise Zajedno wins.

text.p: The German government and parliamentary parties called on Serbian President Slobodan Milosevic on Thursday to recognise opposition victories in municipal polls last November.

During a parliamentary debate on the Balkans in Bonn, all parties expressed sympathy for the opposition "Zajedno" (Together) coalition after Serbian authorities annulled its victories in 14 of 18 major cities and towns.

Foreign Minister Klaus Kinkel praised the tens of thousands of peaceful demonstrators who have kept up two months of protests, and noted that some opposition wins in Belgrade and Nis had now been recognised.
"This must now be implemented," he said. "Declarations alone are not enough. The recognition of the wins in other cities must follow."
Kinkel joined Guenter Verheugen, deputy parliamentary leader of the opposition Social Democrats, in calling on the Serbian opposition to spell out exactly what their policies were.

"The political visions of the opposition in Belgrade often lack clarity on the future position of minorities, particularly the Kosovo (ethnic) Albanians. That is why we want to strengthen our links with the opposition in Belgrade," Kinkel said.
Verheugen criticised the Serbian opposition for failing to take any responsibility for the civil war in Yugoslavia, saying they had represented the same position as Milosevic for too long.
